passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Philips believes the risks set out below are the material risks affecting Philips and its securities. These risk factors may not, however, include all the risks that ultimately may affect Philips. Some risks not yet known to Philips, or currently believed not to be material, may ultimately have a major impact on Philips’ business, revenue, income, assets, liquidity, capital resources, reputation and/or ability to achieve its business and ESG objectives. Please note that this section is not intended to describe risks that have materialized, as these are addressed in other sections and referenced where relevant. Philips defines risks in four main categories: Strategic, Operational, Financial and reporting, and Compliance. Philips presents the risk factors within each category in order of the current view of their expected significance. Compared to the previous year, we have further prioritized risk factors relating to geopolitics and macro-economics, and to AI. We have continued high prioritization of risk factors related to patient safety and quality, supply chain, and the simplification of how we work. Although still relevant, we have de-emphasized risk factors related to global inflation. This does not mean that a lower-listed risk factor may not have a material and adverse impact on Philips’ business, revenue, income, assets, liquidity, capital resources, reputation, and/or ability to achieve its business and ESG objectives. Furthermore, other risk factors not listed below may ultimately prove to have more significant adverse consequences than the listed risk factors. We aim to manage risk within our risk appetite. Pursuing strategic opportunities within the dynamics of the health technology industry typically requires a higher appetite towards the corresponding strategic risks. We may accept considerable strategic risks in a responsible way given the necessity to invest in research and development and to manage the portfolio of businesses to ensure we continually revitalize our offerings. For selected options with very high strategic impact, we may occasionally take a risk-seeking approach subject to careful evaluation. Toward operational risks, we overall take a prudent-to- balanced approach, aiming to optimize productivity and minimize downside risks considering the need for efficient execution, reliable and secure IT systems and continuity of the delivery of our products, services and sustainability commitments. Where operational risks may impact the quality of our products and services and the safety of patients, we take an averse approach. Regarding financial and reporting risks, we adopt a prudent-to-balanced approach aiming at the financial sustainability of the company, investor commitment and stakeholder trust. We manage these risks with the intention of retaining our current strong investment-grade credit rating. As Philips is committed to act with integrity always, we take an averse-to-prudent approach to any risk that would result in breach of compliance with our General Business Principles and mandatory laws and regulations. credit_strengths.text: Operating income recovered sharply across the trend, lifting interest coverage well above the prior year and comfortably above unity, which signals restored earnings capacity to absorb fixed financing charges after the earlier loss-making period.

Gross and net leverage both declined year on year, with net leverage sitting below the next risk-band boundary, leaving meaningful headroom before any downgrade trigger; the indicative financial risk profile is intermediate on this basis.

key_risks.text: Leverage remains above the health care sector median on both gross and net bases, and the operating margin is well below the sector median, so the issuer carries comparatively thinner profitability cushion against its borrowings than peers.

The risk factors emphasize geopolitics, macro-economic shifts, supply chain and patient safety and quality as prioritized exposures for this health technology franchise, each capable of disrupting revenue, liquidity and capital resources across its global operations.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage improved materially year on year and EBITDA coverage of interest is strong in absolute terms, though both sit modestly below the sector median, indicating adequate but not superior debt service headroom relative to peers.

The current ratio improved year on year and exceeds unity, but remains below the sector median, and the absence of a tagged operating cash flow figure prevents any assessment of cash conversion against debt or distributions.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative profile is intermediate: leverage is elevated against the sector but trending down, coverage is recovering, and headroom to the next leverage band is adequate; this is an analytical judgement, not a rating or outlook.

The material gap is the missing operating cash flow tag, which blocks free cash flow, cash-to-debt and distribution coverage tests; until resolved, servicing conclusions rest on earnings-based coverage and balance-sheet liquidity alone.

credit_strengths.text: 營運收入沿趨勢大幅回升，令利息覆蓋率遠高於上一年度，並穩居於一以上，顯示在早前虧損期之後，盈利能力已恢復至足以吸收固定融資費用的水平。
總槓桿及淨槓桿均按年下降，淨槓桿處於下一個風險區間邊界之下，在觸發任何降級之前仍有顯著緩衝空間；按此基礎，指示性財務風險狀況為中等。

key_risks.text: 無論按總額或淨額基礎計算，槓桿均高於醫療保健行業中位數，而營運利潤率亦遠低於行業中位數，因此相對於同業，發行人就其借款而言所持的盈利緩衝較為薄弱。
風險因素將地緣政治、宏觀經濟變化、供應鏈，以及病人安全與質素列為此健康科技業務的優先風險敞口，每一項均可能擾亂其全球業務的收益、流動性及資本資源。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年顯著改善，而 EBITDA 對利息的覆蓋在絕對值上屬強勁，惟兩者均略低於行業中位數，顯示相對於同業，償債緩衝屬足夠但並非優越。
流動比率按年改善並高於一，但仍低於行業中位數，而缺乏已標記的營運現金流數字，令吾人無法就現金轉換相對於債務或分派作出任何評估。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性狀況為中等：槓桿相對於行業偏高但呈下降趨勢，覆蓋率正在恢復，而距下一個槓桿區間的緩衝屬足夠；此乃分析判斷，並非評級或展望。
重大缺口在於缺少營運現金流標記，因而阻礙自由現金流、現金對債務及分派覆蓋率的測試；在解決之前，償債結論僅能依賴以盈利為基礎的覆蓋率及資產負債表流動性。
